routing_table.rule: Start with local instructions/state, then verify before completion claims.
Clarify design first; use TDD once implementation starts.

routing_table.task: Bug, failing test, or unexpected behavior
routing_table.rule: Reproduce and isolate before fixing; add a regression test for code changes.
Use premium automotive direction first; use no-slop gate before handoff.

routing_table.task: Shopify full site or page build
routing_table.rule: Use build orchestrator for execution and full auditor before calling done.

routing_table.task: Product, hero, collection, or marketing images
routing_table.rule: Find exact source-traceable assets first; generate or produce only when needed.

routing_table.task: Automotive film PDP, TDS, specs, or warranty
routing_table.rule: Never invent specs; audit PDP/image/title consistency after edits.

routing_table.task: B2B wholesale funnel or dealer intake
routing_table.rule: Keep price isolation and wholesale flow clear.
Use browser evidence and screenshots for user-facing changes.
Report findings without mutating unless explicitly authorized.

conflict_risks.name: agent-browser
conflict_risks.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents. Use when the user needs to interact with websites, verify dev server output, test web apps, navigate pages, fill forms, click buttons, take screenshots, extract data, or automate any browser task. Also triggers when a dev server starts so you can verify it visually.

conflict_risks.name: agent-browser-verify
conflict_risks.description: Automated browser verification for dev servers. Triggers when a dev server starts to run a visual gut-check with agent-browser — verifies the page loads, checks for console errors, validates key UI elements, and reports pass/fail before continuing.

conflict_risks.name: ai-gateway
conflict_risks.description: Vercel AI Gateway expert guidance. Use when configuring model routing, provider failover, cost tracking, or managing multiple AI providers through a unified API.

conflict_risks.name: ai-sdk
conflict_risks.description: Vercel AI SDK expert guidance. Use when building AI-powered features — chat interfaces, text generation, structured output, tool calling, agents, MCP integration, streaming, embeddings, reranking, image generation, or working with any LLM provider.

conflict_risks.name: brainstorming
conflict_risks.markers: must use, before any, do not invoke, hard-gate
conflict_risks.description: You MUST use this before any creative work - creating features, building components, adding functionality, or modifying behavior. Explores user intent, requirements and design before implementation.

conflict_risks.name: chat-sdk
conflict_risks.description: Vercel Chat SDK expert guidance. Use when building multi-platform chat bots — Slack, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, GitHub, Linear — with a single codebase. Covers the Chat class, adapters, threads, messages, cards, modals, streaming, state management, and webhook setup.

conflict_risks.name: control-chrome
conflict_risks.description: Control the user's Chrome browser for tasks that depend on existing Chrome state: tabs, logged-in sessions, or extensions. Prefer purpose-built connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

conflict_risks.name: control-in-app-browser
conflict_risks.description: Control the in-app Browser for opening, navigating, inspecting visible or interactive page state, clicking, typing, screenshots, and local web testing. It can have existing signed-in sessions. For semantic operations on linked resources, prefer a purpose-built connector, API, or CLI when available.

conflict_risks.name: design-taste-frontend
conflict_risks.description: Anti-slop frontend skill for landing pages, portfolios, and redesigns. The agent reads the brief, infers the right design direction, and ships interfaces that do not look templated. Real design systems when applicable, audit-first on redesigns, strict pre-flight check.

conflict_risks.name: end-to-end-quality-auditor
conflict_risks.description: Final quality-audit workflow for completed site, Shopify theme, content, image, automation, and setup tasks. Use when Codex needs to avoid assumptions, inspect finished work from multiple angles, find remaining problems, fix them, re-check, and provide evidence before handing off as done.

conflict_risks.name: figma-generate-design
conflict_risks.description: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, screen, or view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles via search_design_system, imports them, and assembles screens incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.

conflict_risks.name: gpt-taste
conflict_risks.description: Elite UX/UI & Advanced GSAP Motion Engineer. Enforces Python-driven true randomization for layout variance, strict AIDA page structure, wide editorial typography (bans 6-line wraps), gapless bento grids, strict GSAP ScrollTriggers (pinning, stacking, scrubbing), inline micro-images, and massive section spacing.

conflict_risks.name: imagegen-frontend-web
conflict_risks.description: Elite frontend image-direction skill for generating premium, conversion-aware website design references. CRITICAL OUTPUT RULE — generate ONE separate horizontal image FOR EVERY section. A landing page with 8 sections produces 8 images. Never compress multiple sections into one image. Enforces composition variety (not always left-text / right-image), background-image freedom, varied CTAs, varied hero scales (giant / mid / mini minimalist), narrative concept spine, second-read moments, and a single consistent palette across all images. Optimized for landing pages, marketing sites, and product comps that developers or coding models can accurately recreate.

conflict_risks.name: investigation-mode
conflict_risks.description: Orchestrated debugging coordinator. Triggers on frustration signals (stuck, hung, broken, waiting) and systematically triages: runtime logs → workflow status → browser verify → deploy/env. Reports findings at every step.

conflict_risks.name: vercel-sandbox
conflict_risks.description: Vercel Sandbox guidance — ephemeral Firecracker microVMs for running untrusted code safely. Supports AI agents, code generation, and experimentation. Use when executing user-generated or AI-generated code in isolation.

conflict_risks.name: verification
conflict_risks.description: Full-story verification — infers what the user is building, then verifies the complete flow end-to-end: browser → API → data → response. Triggers on dev server start and 'why isn't this working' signals.

conflict_risks.name: verification-before-completion
conflict_risks.description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always

conflict_risks.name: workflow
conflict_risks.description: Vercel Workflow DevKit (WDK) expert guidance. Use when building durable workflows, long-running tasks, API routes or agents that need pause/resume, retries, step-based execution, or crash-safe orchestration with Vercel Workflow.

cleanup_policy: Prefer root-level user skill paths over mirrored gstack subpaths when names are identical.
Use explicit task routing for overlapping design, QA, image, Shopify, and ArmorHue skills.
Strong-gate skills should be treated as process gates, not domain specialists.
Archive duplicates only after checking current references and one full successful run.
